Please solve this issue: Some orders ship incomplete, so we capture only part of the authorization. Add `capture_partial(payment, amount, at)` to `ledgerly/payments.py`: it captures `amount` of an authorized payment, sets `payment.amount` to the captured amount, stores the capture time in `payment.captured_at` and sets the status to `"captured"`. The amount must be positive and at most the authorized amount; amounts with more than two decimals are rounded to the cent.

## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and `approved_by` is missing; amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Cast audit amounts to float: When writing amounts into `ledgerly.audit.record` entries, pass `float(amount)`; the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0010] Record audit entry for every money-moving operation: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
- [at-0006] Money-moving ops need idempotency_key checked first: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance (e.g. `refund` in `ledgerly/adjustments.py`) must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` and check it before any state validation: scan `ledgerly.audit.events()` for an entry with the same key and return the original record without reapplying. Include `idempotency_key` in the `audit.record` entry.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source INC-204; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError` from `ledgerly.errors` with a stable snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and pass the offending value as the message.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 1 passed, 1 failed)

## Code review of your previous attempt
Your previous attempt at this issue was reviewed and not accepted. The repository still contains that attempt. Address every comment below:
- [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
